extracted.intended_audience: Owners/operators of Public Water Systems (PWS), State/Tribal drinking water agencies, and laboratories performing UCMR testing
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and quality-control standards that PWSs, States/Tribes, and laboratories must follow to implement the Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR), including reporting, sampling, analytical methods, laboratory approval, and data elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and zip code information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information for key individuals (PWS Technical Contact and PWS Official) including name, affiliation, mailing address, phone number and email address within 90 days of EPA notice; update within 30 days of change; one-time reporting of USPS Zip Code(s) for areas served by the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will send a notice requesting contact information. Required timelines: initial response within 90 days, updates within 30 days of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location inventory reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sampling location inventory information by December 31, 2022 using EPA's electronic data reporting system; report updates (including new sources and sampling locations put into use before or during the UCMR sampling period) within 30 days of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record all data elements listed in Table 1 (paragraph (e)) on each sample form and sample bottle as appropriate; send information per sampling kit instructions (which include due date and return address). Report changes to data elements 1–9 by emailing an explanation of the nature and purpose of the proposed change to EPA as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 1: Public Water System Identification (PWSID) Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The code used to identify each PWS. The code begins with the standard 2-character postal State abbreviation or Region code; the remaining 7 numbers are unique to each PWS in the State. The same identification code must be used for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 2: Public Water System Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique name, assigned once by the PWS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 3: Public Water System Facility Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification code established by the State or, at the State's discretion, by the PWS, following the format of a 5-digit number unique within each PWS for each applicable facility (source, treatment plant, distribution system, or other facility). The same identification code must be used for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 4: Public Water System Facility Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique name, assigned once by the PWS, for every facility ID (e.g., Treatment Plant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 5: Public Water System Facility Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Code identifying facility type: CC = Consecutive connection; SS = Sampling station; TP = Treatment plant; OT = Other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 6: Water Source Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of source water for each sampling location. Codes: SW=Surface water; GU=Ground water under the direct influence of surface water; MX=Mixed water; GW=Ground water. Systems must report one code per sampling location reflecting sources used during the 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GU is reported when served all or part by groundwater under direct influence at any time in the 12-month sampling period and not served at all by surface water during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 7: Sampling Point Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification code established by the State or PWS that uniquely identifies each sampling point. Each code must be unique within each facility for each sampling location; use same code for all current and future UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 8: Sampling Point Name
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique sample point name, assigned once by the PWS, for every sample point ID (e.g., Entry Point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 9: Sampling Point Type Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Code that identifies the sampling point location. Example: EP = Entry point to the distribution system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 10: Disinfectant Type
rubrics_metrics.description: All disinfectants/oxidants added prior to and at the entry point to the distribution system. Select all that apply from codes (e.g., PEMB, HPXB, CLGA, CLOF, CLON, CAGC, CAOF, CAON, CLDB, OZON, ULVL, OTHD, NODU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 11: Treatment Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment information associated with the sample point. Select all that apply from codes (e.g., CON, SFN, RBF, PSD, INF, DFL, SSF, BIO, UTR, GWD, PAC, GAC, AIR, POB, MFL, IEX, DAF, CWL, CWA, ADS, OTH, NTU, DKN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 12: Sample Collection Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Date the sample is collected, reported as YYYYMMDD (4-digit year, 2-digit month, 2-digit day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 13: Sample Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: An alphanumeric value up to 30 characters assigned by the laboratory to uniquely identify containers or groups of containers containing water samples collected at the same sampling location for the same sampling date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 14: Contaminant
rubrics_metrics.description: The unregulated contaminant for which the sample is being analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 15: Analytical Method Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification code of the analytical method used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 16: Extraction Batch Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory-assigned extraction batch ID. Must be unique for each extraction batch within the laboratory for each method. For CCC samples report the Analysis Batch Identification Code; for methods without an extraction batch, leave null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 17: Extraction Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Date for the start of the extraction batch (YYYYMMDD). For methods without an extraction batch, leave null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 18: Analysis Batch Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory-assigned analysis batch ID. Must be unique for each analysis batch within the laboratory for each method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 19: Analysis Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Date for the start of the analysis batch (YYYYMMDD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 20: Sample Analysis Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of sample collected/prepared and fortification level. Permitted values include CCCL, CCCM, CCCH, FS, LFB, LRB, LFSM, LFSMD, QCS, FRB, etc., with definitions for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes calibration checks, field samples, QC blanks, fortified samples, duplicates, and other QC sample types used in UCMR monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 21: Analytical Result—Sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator of whether the sample analysis result was '<' (less than; contaminant not detected or below MRL) or '=' (equal to; contaminant detected at the reported measured value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 22: Analytical Result—Measured Value
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual numeric value of the analytical results for field samples and QC sample types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 23: Additional Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Represents the true value or the fortified concentration for spiked samples for QC Sample Analysis Types (CCCL, CCCM, CCCH, QCS, LFB, LFSM, LFSMD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 24: Laboratory Identification Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Code assigned by EPA used to identify each laboratory. Code begins with the two-character State postal abbreviation; remaining five numbers are unique to each laboratory in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 25: Sample Event Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Code assigned by the PWS for each sample event to associate samples with the PWS monitoring plan for EPA tracking. Systems must assign SE1, SE2, SE3, and SE4 for Assessment Monitoring events (SE1/SE2 = first/second sampling period for all water types; SE3/SE4 = third/fourth for SW, GU, MX sources only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must assign a sample event code for each contaminant listed in Table 1. See §141.35(e) Table 1 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 26: Historical Information for Contaminant Detections and Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes/no response for each entry point: Have you tested for the contaminant in your drinking water in the past? If YES, did you modify treatment and if so select types applied (PAC, GAC, IEX, NRO, OZN, BAC, MFL, UVL, OTH, NMT). NO = Have never tested; DK = Do not know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data element 27: Potential PFAS Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes/no answer for each entry point: Are you aware of any potential current and/or historical sources of PFAS that may have impacted drinking water sources? If YES, select all applicable source codes (e.g., MB, FT, AO, CW, PS, WM, HW, UW, SC, MF, FP, TA, PP, CC, PR, MM, CE, FM, PC, FF, OG, UT, CT, OT). NO = Not aware; DK = Do not know.

rubrics_metrics.name: General applicability of monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section applies to PWSs subject to UCMR monitoring as specified in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2). Definitions for PWS population served, State, PWS Official, PWS Technical Contact, and finished water apply per §141.35(a). Determination of whether a PWS is required to monitor is based on system type and retail population indicated by SDWIS/Fed on Feb 1, 2021 or subsequent State corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe your applicability status is different than EPA's notification letter or you are subject to UCMR and were not notified, you must report to EPA as specified in §141.35(b)(2) or (c)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for transient non-community systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If you own or operate a transient non-community water system, you are not subject to monitoring requirements in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability for community and non-transient non-community systems — large systems (>10,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retail PWSs (other than transient non-community) serving more than 10,000 people must monitor according to paragraph (a)(2)(i). If you serve >10,000, you are required to perform Assessment Monitoring (List 1) regardless of notification status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you dispute your applicability you must report to EPA per specified provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large systems — Assessment Monitoring (List 1) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Large systems must monitor for contaminants on List 1 (Assessment Monitoring) per Table 1 (paragraph (a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required regardless of whether you have been notified by State or EPA if you serve a retail population of more than 10,000 people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large systems — Screening Survey (List 2) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 10,001 to 100,000 people must monitor List 2 contaminants if notified by EPA/State that they are part of the State Monitoring Plan for Screening Survey. Systems serving more than 100,000 people must conduct Screening Survey testing regardless of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large systems — Pre-Screen Testing (List 3) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must monitor for contaminants on List 3 if notified by your State or EPA that you are part of Pre-Screen Testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small system monitoring provisions and EPA support
rubrics_metrics.description: For PWSs serving ≤10,000 people that are selected to conduct monitoring, EPA will provide sample containers, pre-paid air bills for shipping materials, conduct laboratory analysis, and report and review monitoring results. If EPA/State will collect samples, you must assist in identifying sampling locations and in collecting samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling schedule and compliance with assigned schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples must be collected according to the schedule assigned by EPA or State, or the schedule you revised using EPA's electronic reporting system on or before Dec 31, 2022. Your schedule must follow timing and frequency in Tables 1 and 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact EPA if you believe you cannot collect samples according to your schedule as specified in §141.35(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection period for List 1 (and applicable List 2/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect samples in one continuous 12-month period for List 1 Assessment Monitoring (and, if applicable, for List 2 or List 3) during timeframe in column 6 of Table 1 (paragraph (a)(3)). EPA or State will specify month(s) and year(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency by contaminant and source type (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For List 1 contaminants: surface water, mixed, or GWUDI: monitor four consecutive quarters (sample events 3 months apart). Ground water: monitor twice in a consecutive 12-month period (5–7 months apart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example timing provided (e.g., Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct for quarterly schedule). Systems must assign sample event codes for each contaminant and event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location requirements (EPTDS and representative connections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect samples at each sample point specified in Table 1 column 5 and footnote c. Samples must be at PWS entry points to the distribution system (EPTDSs) after treatment, representing each non-emergency water source in routine use over the 12-month monitoring period. For purchaser systems with multiple connections from same wholesaler, select one representative connection (highest annual volume); if not available, sample an alternate highest-volume connection. GW systems with multiple EPTDSs may request EPA/State approval to sample representative EPTDS(s) per §141.35(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling instructions and no compositing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the sampling procedure for the method specified in Table 1 column 3 for each contaminant. Do not composite (combine, mix, or blend) samples; collect and preserve each sample separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection and shipping timing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect samples early enough in the day to allow overnight delivery to the laboratory. Do not collect samples on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday because shipping/receipt at required temperature may be compromised unless special arrangements are made with the lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods and reporting at or above MRLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the respective analytical methods specified in Table 1 column 3 for each contaminant; report values at or above the Minimum Reporting Levels (MRLs) specified in Table 1 column 4; and conduct the quality control procedures specified in paragraph (a)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory errors or sampling deviations — resampling requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If laboratory data do not meet required QC criteria (paragraph (a)(5)) or required sampling procedures were not followed (paragraph (a)(4)), you must resample within 30 days of being informed or becoming aware. Resampling is to correct the error, not to confirm previous results. All systems must report results from the first sampling for each sampling period except for cases of sampling or laboratory errors. No samples are to be recollected solely to confirm previous results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory approval requirement for UCMR testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must be certified under §141.28 for one or more compliance analyses; demonstrate for each analytical method they can meet Initial Demonstration of Capability (IDC) requirements in the method documents; and successfully participate in the UCMR Proficiency Testing (PT) Program for each method. Approval decisions are method-specific and contingent on capability to post monitoring data to EPA's electronic reporting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To participate in the UCMR Laboratory Approval Program, labs must register and complete application materials by Aug 1, 2022. Correspondence address and email provided (UCMR_Lab_Approval@epa.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and reporting of results by PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving laboratory results, you must review, approve, and submit system information, sample collection data, and test results. Report results as provided in §141.35(c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small systems: sample kits handling and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Store and maintain sample collection kits sent by the UCMR Sampling Coordinator per kit instructions. Kits include containers, packing materials and cold packs, instructions for collecting the sample and sample treatment, report forms, laboratory contact, and a prepaid return shipping docket and label. Notify the UCMR Sampling Coordinator if materials are missing or damaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small systems: sampling forms and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Completely fill out each sampling form and bottle sent by the UCMR Sampling Coordinator, including data elements listed in §141.35(e) for each sample; sign and date the sampling forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small systems: sampling deviations reporting and resampling procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not collect a sample according to provided instructions, report the deviation within 7 days of scheduled monitoring on the sample reporting form (§141.35(d)(2)). Resample following instructions sent by the UCMR Sampling Coordinator or State. A copy of the form must accompany recollected samples to the laboratory and UCMR Sampling Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small systems: collection and shipping duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect samples at times specified by State or EPA; follow timing and frequency in Table 1 and frequency in Table 2. Once samples and forms are complete, send to the laboratory designated on the air bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control requirements for systems >10,000 population
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving more than 10,000 must ensure the quality control requirements listed are met during sampling procedures and by the analyzing laboratory. All method QC procedures and all UCMR QC procedures must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample collection/preservation quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow sample collection and preservation requirements for the specified method for each contaminant in Table 1. These requirements specify sample containers, collection, dechlorination, preservation, storage, sample holding time, and extract storage and/or holding time that must be assured for the laboratory to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Minimum Reporting Level (MRL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MRL is defined by EPA as the quantitation limit achievable, with 95 percent confidence, by 75 percent of laboratories nationwide, assuming use of good instrumentation and experienced analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratories must be capable of quantifying each contaminant at or below the MRL specified in Table 1 column 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of laboratory performance at or below the MRL — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must validate they can quantify each analyte at or below the MRL by completing and filing records of two procedures: (1) an Initial Demonstration of Capability (IDC) involving replicate analyses at or below the MRL; and (2) for each day UCMR analyses are conducted, a validation of its ability to quantify each contaminant at or below the MRL following specified procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of both procedures must be on file and available for PWS inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration curve and regression model restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The MRL (or concentration below it) used to evaluate performance must be within the range of calibration. The calibration curve regression model and the range of calibration levels used in performance validation must be used in all routine sample analyses. Only straight line or quadratic regression models are allowed; weighted or unweighted models permitted; cubic regression models are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication requirement for IDC
rubrics_metrics.description: Replicate analyses of at least seven (7) fortified samples in reagent water must be performed at or below the MRL for each analyte, and processed through the entire method procedure (including extraction where applicable and with all preservatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction Interval of Results (PIR) calculation and validation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a Prediction Interval of Results (PIR) based on the estimated mean and standard deviation of results using Student's t with appropriate degrees of freedom and confidence level. Determine Half Range PIR (HRPIR) and PIR per specified equations (and Table 3 constant factors). Convert lower and upper PIR limits to percent recovery of the concentration tested. To pass at a level, PIR lower recovery limits cannot be lower than 50% and PIR upper recovery limits cannot be greater than 150%. If PIR recovery limits fall outside 50–150%, laboratory performance is not validated at that concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 provides constant factors (C) to multiply standard deviation for replicates 7–10 at 99% confidence. Required elements for calculation include number of replicates, Student's t value for a two-sided 99% confidence, mean of replicates, and sample standard deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control requirements for validation at or below the MRL (paragraph (a)(5)(iii)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The calibration curve regression model and range of calibration levels used in performance validation must be used in routine sample analysis; only straight line or quadratic regression models allowed; weighted or unweighted models permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph cross-references procedural QC steps that must be consistently applied between validation and routine analysis.
